text: The exchange of goods services and capital across national borders is
subject: International Business
explanation: International business involves cross border trade and investment.

text: The increasing interconnection of world economies is called
subject: International Business
explanation: Globalisation is the growing integration of economies and markets.

text: A business that operates in multiple countries is called a
subject: International Business
explanation: A multinational company operates and invests in several countries.

text: International business is riskier than purely domestic business
subject: International Business
explanation: Cross border business adds currency political and cultural risks.

text: List the drivers of international business
subject: International Business
correctAnswer: Market seeking resource seeking efficiency seeking and strategic asset seeking motives.
explanation: These motives drive firms to internationalise.

text: Explain the importance of international business
subject: International Business
correctAnswer: International business expands markets diversifies risk accesses resources and technology and enhances competitiveness and growth for firms and nations.
explanation: Cover market expansion and resource access benefits.

text: The theory that nations should produce goods they can make most efficiently is
subject: International Business
options: Absolute advantage|Comparative advantage|Product life cycle|New trade theory
explanation: Adam Smiths absolute advantage holds that nations export what they make most efficiently.

text: The theory that nations should specialise where their opportunity cost is lowest is
subject: International Business
explanation: Ricardo comparative advantage justifies trade on relative efficiency.

text: The Heckscher Ohlin theory explains trade by differences in factor endowments
subject: International Business
explanation: Heckscher Ohlin links trade to relative abundance of factors of production.

text: State the theory of comparative advantage
subject: International Business
correctAnswer: A nation benefits by specialising in goods it produces at a lower opportunity cost and trading for the rest.
explanation: Comparative advantage is the basis of mutually beneficial trade.

text: Explain the mercantilist theory of trade
subject: International Business
correctAnswer: Mercantilism held that a nation gains by maximising exports and minimising imports to accumulate gold and silver treating trade as a zero sum game.
explanation: Cover the export surplus and bullion accumulation doctrine.

text: Exporting goods directly to foreign customers is an entry mode of
subject: International Business
explanation: Exporting is selling goods produced domestically to foreign markets.

text: Granting a foreign firm the right to use technology for a fee is
subject: International Business
explanation: Licensing transfers rights to technology or brand for a royalty.

text: A wholly owned subsidiary is the entry mode requiring the highest investment
subject: International Business
explanation: A wholly owned subsidiary involves full ownership and high commitment.

text: List the modes of entering foreign markets
subject: International Business
correctAnswer: Exporting licensing franchising joint venture and wholly owned subsidiary.
explanation: These modes differ in control investment and risk.

text: Explain the factors determining the choice of entry mode
subject: International Business
correctAnswer: Entry mode choice depends on firm resources market size risk tolerance control desired and host country regulations.
explanation: Cover internal capability and external market factors.

text: The international body that regulates world trade is the
subject: International Business
explanation: The WTO sets and enforces rules of international trade.

text: The institution that provides short term finance for balance of payments problems is the
subject: International Business
explanation: The IMF assists countries with balance of payments support.

text: A tariff is a tax imposed on imported goods
subject: International Business
explanation: Tariffs are taxes on imports used to protect domestic industry.

text: List the types of trade barriers
subject: International Business
correctAnswer: Tariff barriers and non tariff barriers such as quotas subsidies and technical standards.
explanation: Trade barriers divide into tariff and non tariff types.

text: Explain the functions of the World Trade Organization
subject: International Business
correctAnswer: The WTO administers trade agreements provides a forum for negotiation settles disputes and monitors trade policies to ensure free and fair trade.
explanation: Cover rule making dispute settlement and trade monitoring.

text: The policy document that governs Indias exports and imports is the
subject: International Business
explanation: The EXIM policy sets the framework for exports and imports.

text: The document that evidences the contract of carriage in shipping is the
subject: International Business
explanation: The bill of lading is a receipt and contract of carriage.

text: A letter of credit is a guarantee of payment by the importers bank
subject: International Business
explanation: A letter of credit assures the exporter of payment by the bank.

text: List the documents used in export trade
subject: International Business
correctAnswer: Commercial invoice bill of lading certificate of origin and letter of credit.
explanation: These documents complete an export transaction.

text: Explain the objectives of the EXIM policy
subject: International Business
correctAnswer: The EXIM policy promotes exports facilitates imports and balances trade to earn foreign exchange and support economic growth.
explanation: Cover export promotion and trade balance objectives.

text: The price of one currency in terms of another is the
subject: International Business
explanation: The exchange rate is the price of one currency in another.

text: The market where currencies are bought and sold is the
subject: International Business
explanation: The forex market facilitates currency trading.

text: Cultural differences can create barriers in international business
subject: International Business
explanation: Language customs and values differ across countries affecting business.

text: Distinguish between a fixed and a floating exchange rate
subject: International Business
correctAnswer: A fixed rate is set by the government while a floating rate is determined by market demand and supply.
explanation: The difference is who determines the exchange rate.

text: Explain the role of culture in international business
subject: International Business
correctAnswer: Culture shapes consumer behaviour negotiation styles and management practices so firms must adapt products communication and management to local cultures.
explanation: Cover adaptation of marketing and management across cultures.

text: Assertion: A weaker domestic currency boosts exports. Reason: A weaker currency makes domestic goods cheaper for foreign buyers
subject: International Business
options: Both assertion and reason are true and reason explains assertion|Both are true but reason does not explain assertion|Assertion is true but reason is false|Assertion is false but reason is true
explanation: A weaker currency lowers the foreign price of exports raising demand.

text: Match the entry mode to its characteristic
subject: International Business
options: Exporting - lowest investment|Wholly owned subsidiary - lowest control|Licensing - highest investment|Joint venture - no shared risk
explanation: Exporting requires the least investment while a subsidiary gives full control.

text: The global institution that lends for long term development projects is the
subject: International Business
explanation: The World Bank finances long term development projects.

text: The set of agreements promoting free trade among member countries is a
subject: International Business
explanation: A free trade area removes barriers among members.

text: Explain the stages of internationalisation of a firm
subject: International Business
correctAnswer: Firms internationalise through stages from exporting and licensing to joint ventures and wholly owned subsidiaries increasing commitment and control at each step.
explanation: Trace the escalation of commitment across stages.

text: Read the case: A firm exporting goods faces payment risk from a foreign buyer. Recommend a payment mechanism that reduces the risk
subject: International Business
correctAnswer: The firm should use an irrevocable letter of credit where the buyers bank guarantees payment against compliant documents.
explanation: Apply the letter of credit to mitigate payment risk.

text: Read the case: A company plans to enter a foreign market but lacks capital and local knowledge. Recommend an entry mode and justify it
subject: International Business
correctAnswer: A joint venture or licensing is best because it shares capital and risk and taps the local partners market knowledge.
explanation: Match limited resources to a shared risk entry mode.

text: Explain the advantages and disadvantages of globalisation
subject: International Business
correctAnswer: Globalisation expands markets lowers costs and spreads technology but also increases competition interdependence and inequality between countries.
explanation: Balance economic integration benefits against its costs.

text: The risk that a foreign government may seize assets is political risk
subject: International Business
explanation: Political risk includes expropriation and policy changes abroad.

text: Explain the factors affecting exchange rates
subject: International Business
correctAnswer: Exchange rates are affected by inflation interest rates balance of payments political stability and market speculation.
explanation: Cover economic and political determinants of exchange rates.

text: List the risks in international business
subject: International Business
correctAnswer: Political risk commercial risk currency risk and cultural risk.
explanation: These risks make international business more complex.

text: Explain the meaning and importance of balance of payments
subject: International Business
correctAnswer: The balance of payments records all external transactions and reveals a countrys trade position currency pressures and need for policy adjustment.
explanation: Cover the current and capital accounts and their significance.

text: The term FOB means the seller bears cost up to the ship named by the buyer
subject: International Business
explanation: FOB means free on board where the seller delivers goods on board the vessel.

text: Explain the role of export promotion councils in India
subject: International Business
correctAnswer: Export promotion councils assist exporters with market information trade fairs quality and policy inputs to boost exports of specific products.
explanation: Cover the support functions of export councils.

text: A company whose global strategy adapts products to each local market follows
subject: International Business
explanation: Localisation adapts offerings to local preferences and conditions.

text: Explain the concept and types of trade blocs
subject: International Business
correctAnswer: Trade blocs range from free trade areas and customs unions to common markets and economic unions with increasing integration among members.
explanation: Describe the levels of regional economic integration.

text: The duty levied on imports to protect domestic industry is a protective tariff
subject: International Business
explanation: Protective tariffs shield domestic producers from foreign competition.

text: Explain the stages of economic integration
subject: International Business
correctAnswer: Economic integration proceeds from free trade area and customs union through common market to economic union with increasing harmonisation of policies.
explanation: Trace the progression of integration stages.

text: Explain the factors that determine international competitiveness
subject: International Business
correctAnswer: Competitiveness depends on cost quality technology innovation and supporting institutions as captured in Porters diamond of factor conditions demand and related industries.
explanation: Cover cost technology and Porters diamond determinants.
